key_insight: Magnesium alloy welding is constrained by crack susceptibility, so the field is shifting toward solid-state and optimized hybrid joining methods that improve joint integrity.
engineering_relevance: For lightweight automotive and other weight-critical designs, the review highlights which welding routes are most practical for AZ-series Mg alloys and where process control matters most.
method: Reviewed scientific databases and patents using targeted keywords
Compared fusion, friction, diffusion, explosive, and hybrid welding methods
Assessed process variables, microstructure, mechanical behavior, and joint integrity
evidence_signal: The paper is a literature review synthesizing published studies and patents, with emphasis on observed weld microstructure, defects, and mechanical performance trends rather than new experimental data.
watch_item: Magnesium welding remains highly defect-sensitive, so process parameters and joint design must be tightly controlled to avoid cracking and loss of mechanical integrity.
paper_title: Welding Techniques for Magnesium Alloy Joints: A Comprehensive Review
